memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: On the west will be the divisions of the camp of Ephraim under their standard. The leader of the people of Ephraim is Elishama son of Ammihud... The tribe of Manasseh will camp next to them... then the tribe of Benjamin... All the men assigned to the camp of Ephraim, according to their divisions, number 108,100. They will set out third. - Num 2:18-24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
On the west side stood Ephraim, Manasseh, and Benjamin, ready to set out third. Once again we see God's careful ordering. Every tribe knew its side, its neighbours, and its turn to move. Nothing was left to confusion.

It is worth noticing that Ephraim and Manasseh were the sons of Joseph. Years earlier, Joseph had been sold as a slave, torn from his family, forgotten by his brothers. Yet here his descendants stand as strong tribes, given an honoured place in the camp of God's people. What men meant for evil, God had turned to good (Gen 50:20).

This should encourage anyone who has suffered wrong or walked through painful seasons. God is able to take the broken parts of our story and weave them into something good and lasting. Joseph could never have imagined, in the pit or the prison, that his family line would one day march as tribes of Israel.

God's ordering of our lives often includes seasons we do not understand. But He is always working, always arranging, always faithful.

Trust the God who gave Joseph's sons a place. He has not forgotten you, and He is able to bring good even out of your hardest chapters — as He supremely did through the cross.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Can you look back and see God bringing good from hard times?
- What painful chapter do you need to trust to God today?
- How does Joseph's story give you hope?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You bring good even from painful seasons. Help me to trust You with the parts of my story I do not understand. Amen.
